title: New Granada
capsule: The United Provinces of New Granada (Provincias Unidas de Nueva Granada) was the first federal republic declared across most of modern Colombia, constituted by the Act of Federation of 27 November 1811 after provincial juntas had broken from Spanish authority during the crisis of the Napoleonic invasion of Spain. The confederation was loose and contested — the period is remembered in Colombian historiography as La Patria Boba (the Foolish Fatherland) — with the province of Cundinamarca remaining outside until Simón Bolívar compelled its adhesion in December 1814. A Spanish reconquest force under Pablo Morillo crushed the republic by 3 September 1816, reimposing the Viceroyalty of New Granada; independence was definitively regained after Bolívar's victory at Boyacá on 7 August 1819, and the entity was absorbed into Gran Colombia at the Congress of Cúcuta in 1821.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political boundaries broadly match the former Viceroyalty of New Granada, but effective provincial control was disputed and the federation never held uniform authority across its claimed territory.
